key_insight: DecompRL teaches LLMs to solve harder coding problems by generating modular sub-functions that can be recombined into many candidate solutions, turning a near-impossible monolithic search into a tractable hierarchical one.
engineering_relevance: For practical code synthesis systems, the method shifts effort from expensive GPU sampling to cheaper CPU-side recombination and verification, reducing token cost while expanding the solution space.
method: Use RL to learn hierarchical decomposition of a program into smaller modules.
Train separate implementations for each module and recombine them to form candidate full solutions.
Exploit the combinatorial space of recombinations to boost effective search without proportional GPU cost.
evidence_signal: On LiveCodeBench and CodeContests with Qwen 2.5 7B and Code World Model 32B, DecompRL beats standard and diversity-optimized RL baselines beyond 10^5 tokens per problem and cuts GPU token cost by about 50x.
watch_item: The approach depends on accurate decomposition and reliable CPU evaluation; if modules are poorly factorized or recombination introduces inconsistent interfaces, performance may degrade.
paper_title: DecompRL: Solving Harder Problems by Learning Modular Code Generation
